source: Musai design, 'Status' step three; research/PITFALLS.md Pitfall 17 (a traversal that folds two at a time can silently miss what a full pairwise check would catch)
description: two arguments tie each other on an incomparable point scope, while a third, wider-scoped argument loses specificity to both — a left-to-right fold that only ever compares the running champion against the next candidate would crown one of the first two without ever checking that they tie each other
reasoning: a winner must beat every other surviving argument, not merely the ones a fold happens to compare it against; alpha and beta are pairwise incomparable in scope and equal in weight, so neither dominates the other even though both individually beat gamma on specificity; the two agree, so the claim holds, led by alpha, which beat none it agrees with, and gamma, which both beat, never leads
